widget.solution:
import numpy as np
from math import exp, sqrt


def crr_price(S, K, r, sigma, T, n, kind="call", american=False, q=0.0):
    """CRR binomial price with n steps and dividend yield q."""
    dt = T / n
    u = exp(sigma * sqrt(dt))
    d = 1 / u
    p = (exp((r - q) * dt) - d) / (u - d)
    if not 0 <= p <= 1:
        raise ValueError(f"p = {p:.4f} is outside [0, 1]: use more steps")
    disc = exp(-r * dt)

    def payoff(s):
        return np.maximum(s - K, 0.0) if kind == "call" else np.maximum(K - s, 0.0)

    j = np.arange(n + 1)
    v = payoff(S * u ** j * d ** (n - j))          # the n + 1 leaves
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):                 # step back to today
        v = disc * (p * v[1:] + (1 - p) * v[:-1])
        if american:                               # exercise at step i?
            j = np.arange(i + 1)
            v = np.maximum(v, payoff(S * u ** j * d ** (i - j)))
    return float(v[0])

widget.solution:
import numpy as np
from math import exp, sqrt


def exercise_boundary(S, K, r, sigma, T, n, q=0.0):
    """Highest share price exercised at each step 0..n of an American put
    (nan where no node is exercised). Exercise when K - s > hold value;
    at expiry, every leaf with K - s > 0."""
    dt = T / n
    u = exp(sigma * sqrt(dt))
    d = 1 / u
    p = (exp((r - q) * dt) - d) / (u - d)
    disc = exp(-r * dt)
    out = [float("nan")] * (n + 1)
    j = np.arange(n + 1)
    s = S * u ** j * d ** (n - j)
    v = np.maximum(K - s, 0.0)
    if (K - s > 0).any():
        out[n] = float(s[K - s > 0].max())
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        hold = disc * (p * v[1:] + (1 - p) * v[:-1])
        j = np.arange(i + 1)
        s = S * u ** j * d ** (i - j)
        hit = K - s > hold                       # exercise beats holding
        if hit.any():
            out[i] = float(s[hit].max())
        v = np.maximum(hold, K - s)
    return out

screens.title: The American rule
screens.prose: Your tree, as rules. With $u = e^{\sigma\sqrt{\Delta t}}$, $d = 1/u$ and $p = \frac{e^{(r-q)\Delta t} - d}{u - d}$, each node keeps $$V = \max\left(e^{-r\Delta t}\left[pV_{\text{up}} + (1-p)V_{\text{down}}\right],\ \text{exercise value}\right).$$ At the money odd and even trees bracket the limit; away from it the error still shrinks like $1/n$ but wanders.
screens.question: On a share with no yield, when does the tree exercise an American call early?

options.text: Never: it equals the European call
Deep in the money, as for the put
options.why: You carried the put's rule over. A call's holder pays $K$ on exercise, and paying early only loses interest.

options.text: One step before expiry, when little time is left
options.why: Holding is worth at least $S - Ke^{-r\Delta t}$, which beats $S - K$ while $r > 0$.

feedback.correct: With no yield the call is never exercised early: test 7 checked that.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the hold value's floor, $S - Ke^{-r\Delta t}$, with $S - K$.

explain.text: A call's hold value is at least $S - Ke^{-r\Delta t}$, more than $S - K$ when $r > 0$. A yield breaks this: the holder misses dividends while waiting. That is why the 5% yield gave the call a premium of 89p.

ideas: `crr_price` grows the share at $r - q$ in $p$, discounts at $r$, and for American options keeps $\max(\text{hold}, \text{exercise})$ at every node.
At the money, odd and even trees bracket Black-Scholes: 500 and 501 steps give £10.4466 and £10.4541 for the £10.4506 call, and their average £10.4503.
The six-month 95 put is worth £3.91 European and £4.01 American; a yield gives deep in-the-money calls a premium too (£30.39 against £29.50 at 5%).
